course_name_original: Sistemas mecánicos en máquinas y vehículos
course_name_en: Mechanical Systems in Machines and Vehicles

learning_outcomes.text: Solve physical problems and their formulation by analyzing the interaction with reality, applying acquired theoretical and practical knowledge.
Be able to perform analysis of each case presented when designing mechanical systems in Machines and Vehicles.
Knowledge of the principles of theory of machines and mechanisms.
Knowledge and skills for the calculation, design, and testing of machines.
Knowledge and skills for the application of materials engineering.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, abilities, and skills in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Characterizes and calculates braking, transmission, speed variator, and spring systems.
Designs and calculates vehicle systems, components, and elements.
Knows and applies the principles of Analysis and Calculation of Vehicle and Machine Systems.
Knows and applies the regulations applicable to Vehicles.
Knows and understands the fundamental principles on which general mechanical systems and main vehicle elements are based.
Knows and understands the interaction between mechanical systems, the vehicle, and its environment.
Understands the specific characteristics of different types of mechanical systems and vehicles and their adaptability for the transport of people and goods.
Knows the advantages and disadvantages of using different materials in mechanical systems, as well as the constructive aspects involved in using one or another.

syllabus_topics: Block I: Mechanical Systems in Automobiles
Block II: Mechanical Systems in Machines
3. Reducers and speed variators, belt and pulley transmission, power screws, and chain.

assessment_methods.method: Global written assessment test (theoretical-practical questions and problems)

assessment_rules: In each call, a global written assessment test will be conducted, which may include both theoretical-practical questions and problems. In the joint global assessment test, each block will have a weight of 50% of the total grade. The course is passed with an overall grade of 5 out of 10. The use of unauthorized materials or electronic devices during the evaluation test may lead to the withdrawal of the exam and a failing grade ('0').
